title: Bluejay × AssemblyAI: Test Voice Agents Built on the Voice Agent API
summary: Bluejay and AssemblyAI have partnered so builders on the Voice Agent API can natively test their agents. The announcement — and the complete runbook for your first simulated calls.
body_markdown:
## 01


Clone and configure


Everything lives in one repository:` AssemblyAI/bluejay-aai-bridge` . Clone it, install the requirements, and copy the example environment file.


** ** ** shell


```text
$   git clone https://github.com/AssemblyAI/bluejay-aai-bridge
$   cd bluejay-aai-bridge
$   pip install -r requirements.txt
$   cp .env.example .env    # add ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY and AGENT_ID
```


Your agent ID is in the agent’s dashboard URL. That’s the whole configuration: the bridge answers as whichever agent you point it at.


Tip


Prefer editing your agent as a file?` python import_agent.py <agent-id>` pulls it down locally, and` AGENT=<name> python bridge.py` runs the bridge against your editable copy — handy for iterating on prompts between test runs.


## 02


Rehearse locally


Before any real simulations, make sure the plumbing holds. The repo ships with` call.py` , a miniature caller that places a short conversation against the bridge on your machine.


** ** ** shell · two terminals


```text
$   python bridge.py             # terminal 1: the bridge
$   python call.py --seconds 12  # terminal 2: a 12-second test call
```


Feed it audio files or plain text, and adjust its` --delay` flag to rehearse barge-in timing. If the twelve-second call comes back clean, your agent just survived its first simulated caller.


## 03


Host the bridge


Bluejay’s Digital Humans call in from the cloud, so the bridge needs a public` wss://` endpoint — secured with Basic-auth credentials, because an open bridge would let anyone run sessions on your API key.


** ** ** .env


```text
CHIRP_USER=bluejay
CHIRP_PASS= <a long random string>
```


One-click deploys are prewired for **Railway** and **Render** , with credentials auto-generated on Render. Anywhere else, just run the Python process: it is stateless, shares nothing between calls, scales horizontally, and answers health checks at` GET /health` .


Watch out


Two hosting mistakes cost real debugging time: instances that **sleep when idle** (the cold start times out the incoming call) and instances sized below the **concurrent sessions** your experiments will open. Always-on, sized for your suite.


## 04


Connect Bluejay


In[Bluejay](https://app.getbluejay.ai/auth/sign-up) , create an agent with connection type **Websocket** and point it at` wss://<your-host>/voice` with the credentials from step 03. That single agent entry is the handshake: from here, everything on the[platform](https://getbluejay.ai/platform) applies to your Voice Agent API agent — generated test scenarios, custom metrics, red teaming, multilingual callers, and monitoring.


## 05


Run and review


Run your first experiment. Every simulated conversation is scored in Bluejay, and the AssemblyAI side keeps its own record of each session — the repo’s` sessions.py` lists and downloads them.


** ** ** shell


```text
$   python sessions.py                # recent Voice Agent API sessions
$   python sessions.py sess_abc123    # download one session
```


Set a` BLUEJAY_API_KEY` and the bridge cross-links each AssemblyAI session ID to its Bluejay result: the scored evaluation on one side, the session-level view of what your agent did on the other. One call, both perspectives.


Cost note


Every simulated call is a **real, billable Voice Agent API session** — by design, because that is what makes the results trustworthy. The bridge terminates sessions cleanly at hangup so nothing billable lingers, and the credentials from step 03 keep strangers off your key.


## Configuration reference


Six variables cover the whole bridge. The[AssemblyAI docs](https://www.assemblyai.com/docs/voice-agents/voice-agent-api/test-with-bluejay) keep the canonical list.


Variable What it does


ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY Required. The account that runs — and is billed for — every session.


AGENT_ID / AGENT Which agent answers: a dashboard agent ID, or the name of a local file imported with` import_agent.py` .


CHIRP_USER, CHIRP_PASS Basic-auth credentials the bridge requires from callers. Set both on any hosted instance.


BLUEJAY_API_KEY Optional. Cross-links each AssemblyAI session ID to its Bluejay simulation result.


LOG_LEVEL` INFO` by default;` DEBUG` narrates every event crossing the bridge.


PORT Where the bridge listens. Defaults to` 8767` .


## Start testing your agent


The integration is live today. The docs, the bridge, and a free Bluejay account are all you need to put your Voice Agent API agent through its first hundred calls.
